title: Adjunction-unit defect criterion on finite triangulated generators
statement:
Let $\mathcal T,\mathcal U$ be triangulated categories with integer shifts, and let $F:\mathcal T\to\mathcal U$ and $U:\mathcal U\to\mathcal T$ be exact functors [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Give an adjunction $F\dashv U$, meaning natural bijections $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal U}(FP,Y)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(P,UY)$, and write $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to UF$ for its unit (the adjuncts of the identity morphisms). Assume these bijections and the unit commute with the specified shift comparisons. Let $\mathcal G$ be any class of objects of $\mathcal T$ and let $\mathcal T_0$ be its finite triangulated closure: objects obtained up to isomorphism from zero and finitely many elements of $\mathcal G$ by finitely many integer shifts and distinguished-triangle extensions [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory].

Suppose that for all $G,H\in\mathcal G$, every distinguished triangle
$$H\xrightarrow{\eta_H}UFH\longrightarrow Q_H\longrightarrow H[1]$$
satisfies $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(G,Q_H[n])=0$ for all $n\in\mathbf Z$. Then for all $P,Q\in\mathcal T_0$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$ the map induced by the specified functor
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal T}(P,Q[n])\xrightarrow{F}\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal U}(FP,FQ[n])$$
is bijective. Under the adjunction this map is exactly $f\mapsto\eta_{Q[n]}\circ f$, with the specified shift comparisons. In particular $F|_{\mathcal T_0}$ is fully faithful, and its replete essential image is a full triangulated subcategory of $\mathcal U$. More explicitly, every morphism between image objects lifts to a source morphism and every distinguished cone triangle on that morphism is isomorphic to the image of a distinguished source triangle. If $\mathcal U_0\subseteq\mathcal U$ is any full replete triangulated subcategory and this restricted functor has essential image $\mathcal U_0$, its equivalence onto $\mathcal U_0$ has an exact quasi-inverse. The statement includes $\mathcal G=\varnothing$ and zero generators; it requires no closure under infinite sums or direct summands.

proof.text: Write $b_{P,Q,n}$ for the displayed map, including $F(Q[n])\cong(FQ)[n]$. By naturality of the adjunction bijection in its first variable, the adjunct of $F(f):FP\to F(Q[n])$ is the adjunct of $1_{F(Q[n])}$ precomposed with $f$, namely $\eta_{Q[n]}\circ f$. This proves the claimed identification for every $P,Q,n$, independently of the vanishing hypothesis. The assumed shift compatibility identifies the shifted unit $\eta_H[n]$ with $\eta_{H[n]}$.

source.place: Agent adjunction calculation; definition of the unit and naturality of the given Hom bijections

proof.text:
Fix $G,H\in\mathcal G$ and choose a distinguished cone triangle of $\eta_H$, which exists by TR1 in [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] to its shifts and rotations. The resulting exact segment is
$$\operatorname{Hom}(G,Q_H[n-1])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(G,H[n])\xrightarrow{\eta_H[n]\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}(G,(UFH)[n])\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(G,Q_H[n]).$$
Both end groups vanish by hypothesis, so the middle arrow is bijective: exactness gives surjectivity at its target and zero kernel at its source. By Step 1 and the adjunction bijection, $b_{G,H,n}$ is bijective for every integer $n$. No claim that $Q_H$ lies in $\mathcal T_0$, or that $\eta_H$ is an isomorphism in the ambient category, is used. Lean shifts of triangles multiply their arrows by (-1)^n. In the injectivity argument use exactness of the inverse rotation and vanishing into Q_H[n-1]; in the surjectivity argument apply exactness to (-1)^n times the desired arrow and cancel this unit. Transport across the composite functor shift isomorphism using Adjunction.unit_app_shift_commShiftIso_inv_app, then cancel the adjunction Hom equivalence.

source.place: Tag 0149, lemma-representable-homological; TR1 and shifts of the unit triangle

proof.text:
Fix $G\in\mathcal G$. Let $\mathcal S_G$ be the class of objects $Q$ for which every $b_{G,Q,n}$ is bijective. It contains zero since $F$ is additive, and it is replete and closed under shifts by the specified shift comparisons and reindexing $n$. If $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ is distinguished with $A,C\in\mathcal S_G$, [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] applied to shifts and rotations gives the exact five-term row
$$\operatorname{Hom}(G,C[n-1])\to\operatorname{Hom}(G,A[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(G,B[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(G,C[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(G,A[n+1]).$$
Exactness of $F$ gives the analogous target row. Functoriality and the natural shift comparisons give a commuting diagram whose vertical arrows are the five maps $b$. Four are bijective by the hypothesis on $A,C$, so [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] in abelian groups makes $b_{G,B,n}$ bijective. Thus $\mathcal S_G$ is a full triangulated class as in [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Step 2 puts every generator in it. Induction on the finite construction of an object of $\mathcal T_0$ therefore gives $\mathcal T_0\subseteq\mathcal S_G$. Lean realization: use the already proved covariant and contravariant Hom diagram chases in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Triangulated.FullyFaithfulGenerator, specifically Functor.homBijectiveShiftsRight and Functor.homBijectiveShiftsLeft and their IsTriangulated and IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms instances. These prove the five-lemma conclusion directly from representable exactness without invoking an abelian-category five-lemma theorem. Apply the stated least-subcategory universal property in each variable; no assumption that a single object generates is made.

source.place: Tag 0149, lemma-representable-homological, and Tag 05QB, homology.tex lemma-five-lemma; first finite induction

proof.text:
Now fix $Q\in\mathcal T_0$. Let $\mathcal R_Q$ consist of $P$ for which every $b_{P,Q,n}$ is bijective. As above zero, isomorphisms and shifts preserve this condition, using $\operatorname{Hom}(P[r],Q[n])\cong\operatorname{Hom}(P,Q[n+(-r)])$. For a distinguished $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$, [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] and rotations give the exact row
$$\operatorname{Hom}(A[1],Q[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(C,Q[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(B,Q[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,Q[n])\to\operatorname{Hom}(C[-1],Q[n]).$$
Applying $F$ gives the target row; the diagram commutes because $F$ preserves composition and the shift comparison is natural. If $A,C\in\mathcal R_Q$, the outer four maps are bijective, hence so is the middle one by [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma]. Thus $\mathcal R_Q$ is triangulated [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Step 3 puts all $G\in\mathcal G$ in it, so a second induction on finite constructions puts all of $\mathcal T_0$ in it. This proves every claimed $b_{P,Q,n}$ is bijective, and at $n=0$ proves full faithfulness of the specified restriction. Lean realization: use the already proved covariant and contravariant Hom diagram chases in WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Triangulated.FullyFaithfulGenerator, specifically Functor.homBijectiveShiftsRight and Functor.homBijectiveShiftsLeft and their IsTriangulated and IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms instances. These prove the five-lemma conclusion directly from representable exactness without invoking an abelian-category five-lemma theorem. Apply the stated least-subcategory universal property in each variable; no assumption that a single object generates is made.

source.place: Tag 0149, lemma-representable-homological, and Tag 05QB, homology.tex lemma-five-lemma; second finite induction

proof.text: Let $a:FP\to FQ$ with $P,Q\in\mathcal T_0$. Step 4 uniquely lifts $a$ to $f:P\to Q$. Choose a distinguished source cone triangle $P\xrightarrow f Q\to R\to P[1]$ by TR1; its third vertex lies in $\mathcal T_0$ by rotations and the closure of [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. Applying exact $F$ gives a distinguished cone triangle on $a$. Given any other distinguished cone triangle on $a$, TR3 in [def-weil-triangulated-category] extends the identities on $FP,FQ$ to a triangle morphism from the image triangle. Its third component is an isomorphism by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso], so this is an isomorphism of triangles. For objects merely isomorphic to $FP,FQ$, first conjugate the arrow by those isomorphisms and use isomorphism invariance of distinguished triangles. This proves the explicit lifting and cone assertion, without uniqueness of the cone isomorphism. In Lean, isoTriangleOfIso₁₂ packages TR3 and Tag 014A after lifting the conjugated arrow and choosing its distinguished cone.

Let $\mathcal I$ be the replete essential image of $F|_{\mathcal T_0}$. It contains zero and is closed under every integer shift by exactness and the shift comparison. Step 5 makes it closed under cones of morphisms between its objects. If $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ is distinguished with $A,C\in\mathcal I$, rotate it to $C[-1]\to A\to B\to C$. Its first two vertices belong to $\mathcal I$, and Step 5 then puts $B$ in $\mathcal I$. Hence $\mathcal I$, as a full replete subcategory, is triangulated by [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory]. These arguments also show that the finite closure $\mathcal T_0$ carries its inherited triangulation. The standard Mathlib instance Functor.essImage.IsTriangulated applies to the full exact restriction T₀.ι ⋙ F.

source.place: TR2 and definition of a full triangulated subcategory, Tag 05QM

proof.text: If $\mathcal I=\mathcal U_0$, corestrict to the full subcategory $\mathcal U_0$. The resulting functor $F_0:\mathcal T_0\to\mathcal U_0$ is exact, fully faithful by Step 4, and essentially surjective by this equality. Apply [lem-trf-fully-faithful-ess-surj-equivalence] to obtain a quasi-inverse $V$ with natural isomorphisms $F_0V\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $VF_0\cong\mathrm{id}$. Categories can be viewed in a common larger universe for this application; no set-sized generating class or infinite categorical limit is required. Use ObjectProperty.lift for the corestriction, lift the essential-image witnesses with ObjectProperty.isoMk, and apply Functor.asEquivalence.

Here are the exactness details for $V$. Write $e:F_0V\cong\mathrm{id}$. Lift, by full faithfulness, the shift isomorphism whose image is
$$F_0(V(Y[1]))\xrightarrow{e_{Y[1]}}Y[1]\xrightarrow{e_Y^{-1}[1]}F_0(VY)[1]\cong F_0((VY)[1]).$$
Its inverse lifts too. Naturality and integer-shift coherence follow by applying faithful $F_0$, where they are precisely the naturality of $e$ and the given shift coherence. Additivity follows similarly. For a distinguished triangle $T$ of $\mathcal U_0$, the triangle $F_0V(T)$ with this comparison is isomorphic via $e$ to $T$. Complete the first arrow of $V(T)$ to a distinguished source triangle $S$ by TR1. TR3 compares $F_0S$ with $F_0V(T)$ by identities on their first two vertices; [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes the third component invertible. Lift that component and its inverse using full faithfulness; faithfulness verifies the triangle equations and the inverse equations. Thus $S\cong V(T)$, so TR1 makes $V(T)$ distinguished. Therefore $V$ is exact. Finally, with no generators (or only zero generators) the finite constructions give only zero objects up to isomorphism; the two inductions still start at zero and all image and inverse arguments still apply. No sum or retract closure has entered any step. Mathlib implements these constructions by Equivalence.commShiftInverse and Equivalence.commShift_of_functor; Adjunction.isTriangulated_rightAdjoint proves exactness of the inverse. The comparison with the specified restriction is ObjectProperty.liftCompιIso, with its canonical NatTrans.CommShift instance.

lean.statement: theorem Adjunction.generator_defect_criterion {C : Type u₁} {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₁} C] [Category.{v₂} D] [HasZeroObject C] [HasZeroObject D] [Preadditive C] [Preadditive D] [HasShift C ℤ] [HasShift D ℤ] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] [Pretriangulated D] [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated C] [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated D] (F : C ⥤ D) (U : D ⥤ C) [F.CommShift ℤ] [U.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated] [U.IsTriangulated] (adj : F ⊣ U) [adj.CommShift ℤ] (G T₀ : ObjectProperty C) [T₀.IsTriangulated] [T₀.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms] (hG : G ≤ T₀) (hT₀ : ∀ (S : ObjectProperty C) [S.IsTriangulated] [S.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms], G ≤ S → T₀ ≤ S) (hdefect : ∀ (G₁ G₂ : C), G G₁ → G G₂ → ∀ (R : C) (g : U.obj (F.obj G₂) ⟶ R) (h : R ⟶ G₂⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧), Triangle.mk (adj.unit.app G₂) g h ∈ distTriang C → ∀ n : ℤ, Subsingleton (G₁ ⟶ R⟦n⟧)) : (∀ (P Q : C), T₀ P → T₀ Q → ∀ n : ℤ, Function.Bijective (fun f : P ⟶ Q⟦n⟧ ↦ F.map f ≫ (F.commShiftIso n).hom.app Q)) ∧ (∀ (P Q : C) (n : ℤ) (f : P ⟶ Q⟦n⟧), adj.homEquiv P (F.obj (Q⟦n⟧)) ((F.map f ≫ (F.commShiftIso n).hom.app Q) ≫ (F.commShiftIso n).inv.app Q) = f ≫ adj.unit.app (Q⟦n⟧)) ∧ Nonempty (T₀.ι ⋙ F).FullyFaithful ∧ (T₀.ι ⋙ F).essImage.IsTriangulated ∧ (∀ (P Q : C), T₀ P → T₀ Q → ∀ (A B Z : D) (eP : F.obj P ≅ A) (eQ : F.obj Q ≅ B) (a : A ⟶ B) (b : B ⟶ Z) (c : Z ⟶ A⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧), Triangle.mk a b c ∈ distTriang D → ∃ (f : P ⟶ Q) (R : C) (g : Q ⟶ R) (h : R ⟶ P⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧), T₀ R ∧ F.map f ≫ eQ.hom = eP.hom ≫ a ∧ Triangle.mk f g h ∈ distTriang C ∧ Nonempty (F.mapTriangle.obj (Triangle.mk f g h) ≅ Triangle.mk a b c)) ∧ (∀ (U₀ : ObjectProperty D) [U₀.IsTriangulated] [U₀.IsClosedUnderIsomorphisms], (T₀.ι ⋙ F).essImage = U₀ → ∃ (E : T₀.FullSubcategory ≌ U₀.FullSubcategory) (_ : E.functor.CommShift ℤ) (_ : E.inverse.CommShift ℤ), E.CommShift ℤ ∧ E.functor.IsTriangulated ∧ E.inverse.IsTriangulated ∧ ∃ e : E.functor ⋙ U₀.ι ≅ T₀.ι ⋙ F, NatTrans.CommShift e.hom ℤ)
